## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Aṭṭhisenakajātaka* (Ja 403) is a canonical Jātaka narrative set during the Buddha's stay at the Aggāḷava shrine near Āḷavī, delivered in connection with rules regarding the construction of monastic cells [SuttaCentral]. The framing story shares its occasion with the *Maṇikaṇṭhajātaka*, in which the Buddha explains that before his advent, non-Buddhist recluses avoided soliciting alms even when extended an open invitation by rulers, viewing begging as inherently unpleasant [SuttaCentral]. In the tale of the past, the Bodhisatta is born as the ascetic Atthisena; when a Pañcāla king is pleased with him and offers him anything up to his kingdom, the sage chooses restraint and silence rather than asking for gifts, prompting a dialogue between them on begging and the sorrow of refusal [Anandajoti 2010; SuttaCentral].

SuttaCentral identifies a full Sanskrit parallel in the *Mahāvastu* (San Lo Mvu 107, *The Jātaka of Asthisena*), along with parallels in the *Sambahulasutta* (SN 9.4) and the Chinese *Saṁyuktāgama* (SĀ 1331 and SĀ2 351) [SuttaCentral]. It also shares a passage-level correspondence with the Vinaya *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* (Saṅghādisesa 6) and is mentioned in the *Milindapañha* (Mil 5.5.9) [SuttaCentral]. Computationally, DharmaNexus records ten matching passages of Pali-internal text reuse with the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (Tatiyo bhāgo), as well as low-scoring cross-language alignments with the Tibetan *Sūtrālaṃkārabhāṣya* (D4026) [DharmaNexus].
